examples.title: Additional properties
examples.reason: Twenty Material/Cupertino mounted cases use the imported inventory fixture on JVM: existing empty and dotted keys edit their exact values and clearing an isolated string keeps the key with its empty-string default; bracket, numeric and whitespace keys stay visible; dotted and whitespace names are stored without splitting or trimming; permitted blank Add creates an exact empty key and then disables on collision without inline draft feedback; explicit local false disables blank Add over global true and restrict keeps minProperties deletes disabled. A focused test-only telemetry UI over the imported schema/data rejects a too-short propertyNames key and accepts a valid one. The imported Inventory section places declared Reference and Quantity before dynamic Warehouse and Handling; editing and renaming Warehouse preserves the other values and exposes rename/delete actions only for dynamic fields. A live English/Bulgarian switch uses the source catalog for the property-name prompt and dynamic actions without writing data; a shared text resolver preserves scoped host overrides before generic source keys. Core tests verify literal, blank and whitespace names plus stale rename/add protection. JVM and iOS simulator mounted cases pass after the isolated-clear fix; Android main compiles. Unfiltered JS/Wasm browser suites pass with zero mounted failures or skips; the focused core cases pass on both targets. Four supplemental Material/Cupertino mounted cases in two pairs verify composed propertyNames with a root $defs reference and a nested local $ref inside an isolated dotted-key value, including parent validity recovery; pure tests verify reference chaining without rewriting default/enum/const JSON values. Sixteen supplemental Material/Cupertino mounted cases verify overlapping numeric pattern bounds in either declaration order, one editor, minimum/maximum error routing on a declared property, renaming into or out of an overlapping pattern while preserving the exact value and updating validity, editing both object fields supplied by two matching structural patterns until the object becomes valid, and correcting an inner dynamic value at ordinary and dotted literal keys inside an outer dynamic object. A dynamic-field error appears once at its field instead of being repeated at the parent. Core tests cover strongest bounds across three matches, structural conjunction, and rendered dynamic-key error scopes. The unfiltered JS/Wasm browser suites pass with zero mounted failures or skips. Remote references, recursive array/object nesting and device interaction remain to verify.

examples.title: Conditional fields: generated and authored layouts
examples.reason: Fifteen Material/Cupertino fixture cases pass on JVM, iOS simulator, JS browser and Wasm browser. They cover generated, inline authored and registered object details, missing data, retained inactive fields excluded from the additional-property editor, visible Bulgarian diagnostics, and a three-way overlapping field whose active maxLength prevents excess input. Registered detail keeps authored groups, including empty groups, through branch changes. Opted-in allOf objects use object projection while anyOf keeps its selector. Branch changes preserve inactive data without incidental writes. Nine core cases pass on all four targets for option precedence, nested allOf, overlapping constraints, null-trigger dependencies, boolean conditions, root $defs references, required markers, additional-property reservation, compile diagnostics and Bulgarian/English fallback. Android main compiles; Android device interaction, Template/Slot branch ownership, remote references and deeper compositions remain unverified

examples.title: Container validation indicator
examples.reason: Twenty-eight Material/Cupertino mounted fixture cases pass on JVM and iOS simulator; the unfiltered JS and Wasm browser suites pass with zero skips. They cover global category aggregation, a collapsed Group indicator and its removal after host repair without a data write, certifications array marker suppression while its own minItems error remains visible, global count opt-in and ValidateAndHide transitions, isolated invalid composite object/array/combinator cells beside valid sibling rows, Contact and Experience detail errors, oneOf and anyOf own-error feedback including the reference aggregate anyOf keyword, allOf phone feedback, English/Bulgarian unbound labels under a live locale switch, a translated data-presence tooltip on keyboard focus and pointer hover, and a minLength pre-touch filter that hides inline text until blur while retaining the Group cue. A test-only Certifications UI variant enables the source-disabled marker and verifies a three-entry structured summary, row context, expansion/collapse, live English/Bulgarian action text and zero writes. The source README requests opening the array marker, but its UI schema explicitly sets showValidationIndicator false. Summary rows now resolve schema titles and ordinary field-label keys; the spec importer creates ordinary field-key aliases from schema-path catalog keys without replacing authored keys. The validator preserves the certificate-name errorMessage key; the source catalog's global error.minLength text takes precedence over it in this fixture. The default error pipeline honors control custom, field keyword, global keyword, then schema message precedence. Six paired edit cases repair Alex’s oneOf branch, anyOf phone tab and allOf phone field; each clears its own cell marker and publishes one committed write. Two paired pre-touch cases keep oneOf/anyOf own errors hidden initially while the cell marker remains, then reveal them after same-branch selection or tab touch without writing data. A separate paired Material/Cupertino mounted test verifies that an AllOf minProperties own error stays hidden before interaction and appears when focus leaves a child field, with no data write. Real-device interaction remains unverified.

examples.title: Label interpolation
examples.reason: Thirty-two mounted Material/Cupertino Label cases pass on JVM, iOS simulator, JS browser and Wasm browser. They mount every imported Label category: static and dynamic parameters, plural/literal braces, Markdown, translated plan/currency/number/date, inert interpolation-off labels, JavaScript-named JSON keys and five author errors. The imported keys and inert labels update with data and a live English-to-Bulgarian locale switch while the reserved locale variable remains available and diagnosed as an invalid parameter name. Only English and Bulgarian are shipped; unsupported locale tags fall back to English. A paired host-translator case verifies the React/Svelte translate(key, fallback) extension: catalog hits win, unknown keys use the authored fallback, and a live Bulgarian switch updates the result. Paired collection cases verify bounded CEL all/exists predicates and filter/map chaining update with host data; pure cases cover map keys, three-argument map, list and string-key JSON map literals, and transform errors. A mounted string-key map literal changes its equality result after host data replacement in both families. Logical AND/OR absorb ordinary operand errors when another operand is decisive. Postfix indexing selects from list/map literals and map/filter results; a mounted filtered first value updates with host data. Receiver-style size(), contains(), startsWith() and endsWith() compose with literals and filtered data, and mounted labels update those results with host data. List concatenation with + composes with size, indexing and macros and updates a mounted indexed result with host data. Portable bool, int and double conversions now handle valid strings, truncation and range errors; mounted converted values update with host data. CEL r/R raw string literals preserve backslashes in quoted text and map keys, including a mounted Label. string() converts string, Boolean and signed integer JSON scalars; dyn() preserves runtime values, and a mounted conversion updates with host data. Triple-quoted CEL strings, including raw multiline forms, parse through template and expression scanners; a receiver call mounts in both renderer families. Finite string(double) uses locale-independent fixed/scientific formatting, preserves signed zero and shortens the minimum subnormal boundary and passes normal/maximum/integer-precision boundaries across targets; the mounted conversion updates with host data. The focused 45 pure and 32 mounted Label cases pass on JVM, iOS simulator, JS browser and Wasm browser. Other cases cover live host config/context and selected list item, closed gates, out-of-range indexes and escaped Markdown substitutions. Full CEL including non-string map keys, additional time-only/instant zone boundaries, fixture form-control interactions and physical-device accessibility remain open
